version.changelog: Initial release: auto-extract memories from conversations

llm.summary: The skill's described purpose (extract and persist conversation memories) is plausible and mostly matches its instructions, but it requests runtime capabilities (FileWrite and sessions_spawn) that are not reflected in the registry metadata and that increase risk — especially because autonomous invocation is allowed — so the inconsistencies and privilege requests warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the runtime instructions: the skill reads the current conversation, extracts short memory items, and writes them to memory/{{date}}.md. Requesting file write access is expected for persistent memory storage. However, the SKILL.md also asks for 'sessions_spawn' (ability to fork a child agent) which is not obviously required for simple extraction-and-write logic and is not reflected elsewhere in the registry metadata — this is disproportionate unless the implementation needs a separate background agent for non-blocking writes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are explicit and scoped: read the current conversation, extract categorized short items, append to a daily markdown file, and post a short notification. There are no external network endpoints or unrelated file reads. The only scope concern is the instruction to run automatically 'every conversation end' and to run in the background (via sessions_spawn) — that broad trigger increases the amount of user data that will be collected and persisted without per-run consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files. No downloads or package installs. This minimizes supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md declares the need for FileWrite and sessions_spawn, but the skill registry metadata (requirements lists) shows no declared credentials or config paths. FileWrite is proportional to the stated purpose, but sessions_spawn is a higher-privilege capability that is not obviously necessary and increases blast radius (child agents could run additional actions). There is also no mention of where memory/ is located or access controls for those files, so sensitive conversation content could be persisted in an uncontrolled location.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false (good), but autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default). Combining autonomous/background execution with sessions_spawn and file writes can enable persistent background activity and accumulation of user data. The skill does not declare limits on how long it stores memory, retention policies, or how to opt out — increasing privacy/privilege concerns.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill does what it says (extracts and stores conversation memories), but before installing you should verify: (1) whether the platform will grant FileWrite and especially sessions_spawn to the skill — sessions_spawn lets it fork child agents and increases risk; (2) where the memory/ directory will live and who can read it (is it encrypted, accessible to other skills or users, backed up); (3) retention and deletion policy for stored memories and whether sensitive user data may be written; (4) whether automatic extraction on every conversation end is acceptable for your privacy needs — consider requiring manual triggers instead; (5) prefer limiting the write scope (restrict to a dedicated, access-controlled path) or disallow sessions_spawn unless justified. If you cannot confirm these runtime controls, treat the skill as risky and consider using a manual/more-audited approach to persistent memories.
